payload.title: Harden hosted CI: pin actions by SHA, least-privilege token, pinned runner
payload.body:
The five workflows under .github/workflows/ use tag-pinned actions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4), ubuntu-latest, no top-level permissions block and no concurrency group. Bring them to the agentbrew and dotfiles model: pin every action by commit SHA with a version comment, pin the runner image (ubuntu-24.04), add top-level 'permissions: contents: read' (widen per job only where needed), add a concurrency group that cancels superseded pull-request runs, set persist-credentials: false on checkout, and add a timeout per job. Keep the gate the same (lint, commands-drift, test, e2e, action-dogfood). Then decide whether the CI jobs join the required-checks ruleset next to claim-check, as the other two repos do. Update docs/release-and-ci.md and AGENTS.md. Found by the 2026-11-10 open-source safety audit; the audit stopped before this step.
- **Hypothesis**: SHA-pinned actions and a read-only default token remove the mutable-tag supply-chain path; unpinned 'uses:' lines in .github/workflows drop from all to 0.
- **Measurement**: grep -rhE '^\s*-?\s*uses: [^.]' .github/workflows | grep -vcE '@[0-9a-f]{40}'
- **Success**: the command prints 0 and every CI job is green on the PR and on main.
- **Pivot**: if a pinned action breaks the gate twice, keep that one action on its tag, record why in docs/release-and-ci.md, and pin the rest.
- **Anchor**: GitHub docs 'Security hardening for GitHub Actions'; OpenSSF Scorecard checks Pinned-Dependencies and Token-Permissions.
